title: A council's roundabout recommendation
bodyMd: Seeking to reduce collisions at a busy intersection, a city council replaced the traffic signal there with a roundabout. In the two years since, collisions reported at that intersection have fallen by forty percent, and the council has now recommended converting eleven similar intersections elsewhere in the city. Critics note that the conversion happened in the same month that a new bypass opened, diverting a substantial share of through traffic away from the intersection, and that the council's forty percent figure counts only those collisions that were reported to the police.
accessibilityText: A short argumentative passage. A city council replaced a traffic signal at a busy intersection with a roundabout. Reported collisions there fell forty percent over the following two years, and the council now recommends converting eleven similar intersections. Critics point out two things: a new bypass opened in the same month and diverted much of the through traffic away from the intersection, and the forty percent figure counts only collisions reported to the police.

provenance.notes: Original argumentative passage written for this question bank. The city, council, intersection and figures are invented and are not drawn from any ETS material or any real municipal report.
